context: Adds a borrowing iterator to the ring buffer so callers can walk it with standard combinators.
explanation: RingBufferIter walks the buffer in logical order starting at head, correctly bounded by len (not the underlying capacity), and yields &T so callers get map/filter/collect/for-loops without seeing the internal Vec<Option<T>> representation. The iterator's lifetime is tied to the borrow of the buffer, which is the right shape for a non-consuming iterator and keeps the existing push API untouched.
